A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDAC/BAL research. The complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite figure renumbering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original continuous-control experiments in Section 5, along with gridworld simulations and additional ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a successor-only bonus-bounding ablation in Figures 4a and 10.

M1.justification: The actor, critic, and temperature losses, bounded TD target, and time-dependent bounding procedure are unchanged. The added experimental variant tests a combination of existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six MuJoCo environments, three Adroit tasks, five DMC dog tasks, and appendix gridworld. The added ablation uses retained task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparison in Figures 4a and 10 adds the variant f=I, g=tanh(x/10), increasing the compared bounding configurations from three to four. The SAC, TD3, X-SAC, and tabular M-VI comparator sets otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 adds a successor-only bounding control, completing the four combinations of enabling or disabling current- and successor-term bounding. Existing training budgets, architectures, metrics, and normalization procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Figures 4a and 10 newly test whether bounding the successor bonus alone is sufficient. The other bounding-function, schedule, clipping-diagnostic, and X-SAC sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain ten-run continuous-control evaluations, bootstrap confidence intervals for aggregate scores, percentile bands for per-environment results, and 100 gridworld initializations. The added ablation uses the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 4a and 10 add results for f=I, g=tanh(x/10), showing near-zero aggregate normalized IQM and poor per-environment learning. The other benchmark results and their reported rankings are retained.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 and Appendix B.5 introduce and derive a g-dependent factor between zero and one in the lower bounds' entropy penalty. Section 4.1 relaxes strict sign constraints to permit zero-valued bounding functions, and Lemma B.12 corrects the stated advantage sign.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: MDAC, benefits of bounding both bonus terms, convergence and inherent-error analyses, and improved benchmark performance. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds an interpretation of condition (11) through entropy reduction and policy change, and explains the refined bound's regularized and unregularized limiting cases. Section 5.1 connects the new ablation to Proposition 2. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2.1 and Tables 1–2 retain the same implementation links, software versions, hyperparameters, hardware, and runtime information. Section 5.2's added H/10 expression restates the existing scheduling rule and numerical value.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Munchausen RL, clipped advantage learning, and other mirror-descent methods are unchanged. Bibliographic URL removals and venue corrections do not change the referenced works.

P1.justification: v3 corrects spelling and grammar, edits the contributions paragraph, expands the convergence explanation, and adds subsection headings within Appendix B.5. The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4a and 10 gain a curve and legend entry; Figure 10 also displays denser trajectories and adjusted axes. Existing bounding-function and Adroit/DMC figures are repositioned and renumbered, with associated text reflow. Table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the existing convergence bound's dependence on g explicit and adds the missing successor-only ablation, improving support for the distinct roles of the two bounding terms. Proof corrections and language editing also help. These are limited gains: the method, benchmark coverage, and fixed-alpha/tabular theoretical limitations remain unchanged.
